extracted.intended_audience: architects, architecture students, art historians, and informed readers interested in medieval and Renaissance architectural ornament
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on designing and judging archivolts, apertures, capitals, and roofs in Italian and Northern Gothic/Renaissance architecture, emphasizing organismal fit, placement of decoration, proportions, and ornament vocabulary. Covers comparative methods (Southern/Byzantine vs Northern), material/color use, and proper/incorrect treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two fundamental architectural 'orders' (Lawful Discipline vs Lawful Freedom)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are only two real orders representative of the two great influences which must forever divide the heart of man: the one of Lawful Discipline (perfection and order, danger of degeneracy into Formalism); the other of Lawful Freedom (vigor and variety, danger of degeneracy into Licentiousness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a high-level evaluative principle when choosing a mode of ornament: disciplined, formal restraint vs free, varied invention. Be mindful of the respective dangers (formalism or licentiousness) in extreme application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornament must follow the natural organism of the arch
rubrics_metrics.description: The arch has a natural organism which separates its ornament into distinct families; therefore decoration of arches should spring from their structural form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the arch-line and arch masonry as having inherent modes of ornament — don't impose arbitrary ornament where the structure has none. Use the arch's form to determine families of mouldings and surface treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lintel has no specific decoration; treat lintel and arch differently
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the mere lintel there is no specific decoration, nor can be; it has no organism to direct its ornament. The arch head, however, has an organism that dictates ornament families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid forcing systematic ornament onto lintels; allow lintels to take ornament according to position or architect's will, but respect the arch's inherent decoration logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile architrave and voussoirs honestly (treaty principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the architrave is entirely banished by the voussoirs, a 'treaty' is often signed: the architrave dismisses its inner lines to leave space for the voussoirs, but in return the architrave may expand its cornice into bolder prominence (even put brackets under it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When combining classical architrave elements with voussoirs, adjust inner mouldings so both can coexist; allow concessions (e.g., expanded cornice) rather than clumsy overlays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not decorate the soffit alone — decorate the visible outer surface
rubrics_metrics.description: While the outside or vertical surface may properly be decorated and the soffit left plain, 'the soffit is never to be decorated, and the outer surface left plain.' Carving solely under soffits is a misuse of ornament because it is hidden from general view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place primary sculpture where viewers expect and can see it. Carving under soffits is acceptable only in situations people walk beneath (e.g., wagon vaults, arch soffits under passageways); avoid hiding decoration where it cannot be readily perceived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panelled soffits are rational only where people walk beneath them
rubrics_metrics.description: The custom of decorating arch soffits with panelling is a Roman application rational for wagon vaults or arch soffits under which one walks; it is misplaced when applied to windows (people do not walk through windows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the viewer's vantage point justifies soffit ornament; avoid applying interior/roof motifs to exterior openings where they will not be appreciated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Southern/Byzantine archivolt form: decorate outer surface, leave soffit plain
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinctively Southern and Byzantine archivolt (section a, Fig. LXX) is susceptible of almost every species of surface ornament, subject to the law that the outside vertical surface may be decorated while the soffit is left plain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Southern/Byzantine treatment, concentrate sculpture and chasing on the external faces of voussoirs and avoid hidden soffit work; do not invert this relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Northern archivolt development: use deep steps, chamfers, grouped shafts
rubrics_metrics.description: In Northern practice, deep archivolts attain depth by a succession of steps; the richest northern archivolt decoration is based on aggregation of ornament of these several steps, later aided by chamfers and grouped shafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a northern Gothic effect, design multiple concentric or stepped archivolts, chamfer edges, and introduce solid shafts in dark inner angles to enrich shadow and profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chamfering/beading as decisive northern ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: An insidious chamfer (beading/chamfering) can turn the flank of blank archivolts, producing a rich group of deep lines running concentrically with the arch, which effectively ends the dominance of the voussoirs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chamfers and beads to create strong concentric lines and shadow in deep archivolts; understand that excessive chamfering will subordinate voussoirs to the new mouldings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dishonourable treatment of voussoirs (rustication, masks, slicing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voussoirs that 'go over to the classical camp' are often sharply chiselled at the joints, rusticated, or cut into masks and satyrs' heads — treatments criticized as detestable and dishonourable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not display voussoirs in a way that pillories their structural honesty (exaggerated rustication, right-angled steps cutting their limiting line). Preserve the voussoir's sympathy with the arch rather than mutilating it to fit a flat wall aesthetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use color and material in southern Italian Gothic to reconcile elements
rubrics_metrics.description: In southern (Italian) practice, voussoirs and architrave can be reconciled by color (e.g., colored voussoirs, inlaid brick pieces), and careful inlay so 'the color ought not to be let go all at once.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider delicate use of colored brick or stone in voussoirs and inlay at stone angles to moderate color transitions and integrate arch and wall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer magnified-facsimile outer arches to concentric arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple concentric archivolts are used, the nobler method is to make every outer arch a magnified facsimile of the innermost one (each arc including the same number of degrees), rather than drawing concentric arcs that make outer arches nearly round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale the geometry of outer arches proportionally to the inner arch to preserve elegance and springiness; avoid simple concentric arcs that produce heavy, monotonous outer forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greater depth of voussoirs at the top is good construction and decoration
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater depth of the voussoirs at the top of the arch is a feature of good construction and valuable for decoration, helping reconcile outer and inner arch curves in deep archivolts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase voussoir depth toward the crown where structurally and decoratively advantageous to allow graceful transitions among multiple archivolts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jamb ornamentation should parallel archivolt treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Excepting voussoir peculiarities, the same terms used for archivolt treatment may be applied to the jamb; shafts, zigzags, and transverse ornament in jambs are parallel to archivolt treatments and later swept away by canaliculated mouldings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coherence between jamb and archivolt treatments; develop niche and statue decoration in recesses and adapt shafting and mouldings consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracery is essentially multiplication of small archivolts; treat it as such
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracery is a mere multiplication and entanglement of small archivolts, and its cusp ornament is a minor condition of that proper to the spandril.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tracery by considering it as the inner-most group of archivolts bent into foliations; the beauty of tracery bars requires separate, detailed principles and should respond to mechanical/traditional precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior ornament must fit the building's 'proper temper'
rubrics_metrics.description: Exterior ornaments may be at variance with the temper the building intends; interior ornaments are inadmissible if they are at variance because those who enter will be in the proper temper or wish to acquire it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In interiors, choose ornament compatible with the building's intended mood; avoid frivolous, profane, or grotesque subjects that undermine interior expression (though minor grotesques do occur historically).

rubrics_metrics.name: Roof ornamentation: interior structure should inform interior decoration; exterior treatment is subordinate
rubrics_metrics.description: In roofs, the anatomical structure that should guide decoration is visible in the interior only; therefore interior ornament of roofs is both wide and important, while exterior ornament is comparatively subordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let visible structural members of roofs guide interior ornament (vault bosses, ribs, beams). Treat external roof decoration more sparingly and in deference to weathering and external legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of the spur (convex vs concave schools)
rubrics_metrics.description: The spur in convex school: plans generally preferred by sculptors of the convex school with spurs often carved into animal forms and ornament spread over whole mass; concave school: treatment borrowed from original Corinthian — curling tendril or concave leaf with four-sided abacus, apt to become rigid and effeminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose spur treatment consistent with the school's character: convex (broad mass with varied spurs and animal forms) vs concave (Corinthian-derived, delicate tendrils and abaci). Beware concave tendency toward rigidity and meagreness in upper tendrils/abacus.
